title: Known advisories for MCP servers, matched on your machine
body: The tool now knows the published security advisories for MCP servers and agent tools: 144 of them across 32 packages to start with, among them mcp-remote, mcp-atlassian, the reference servers and four packages published with malicious code. For each MCP server in your configs it takes the package and the version it starts (the pinned one, or the one npx last fetched) and checks it against that list. High, critical and malicious ones are reported as affected, so the GitHub Action fails a pull request that adds one; the rest are for review, and so is a package with advisories and no pinned version. The list is compiled from OSV into advisories.json, reviewed and signed with the rest, so the match happens on your machine and no package name is sent anywhere. The watchlist page names every package.

title: An inventory of what your agents can load and run
body: --agents adds one list of everything an AI agent on the machine can load or run: every MCP server with the package and version it starts, whether that version is pinned (and the version npx last fetched if it isn't) or the host of a remote server, every skill and where it came from, every hook, and the permission settings that were flagged, each with its findings. --json FILE writes the findings and this inventory as JSON, for your own tooling. With --osv, each MCP server's package is checked against OSV as well. Names of environment variables and headers are listed, never their values. Sample configs inside package caches are no longer mistaken for real ones.

title: The one-liner checks the release signature before it runs
body: curl | sh now downloads the signatures as well and runs secinspect.py and advisories.json only if both match our release key, which is kept offline. Before this, only installed copies checked it. If a file was changed on the way, or on the site, it stops and says so. A machine with no ssh-keygen, or OpenSSH older than 8.1, can't check; it says that and runs. The line under every table, and the top of the HTML report, now name the release that produced the result: its date, the script's hash and whether it is the signed one. Each release's hashes also go into Sigstore's public log through GitHub's artifact attestations, so you can check a downloaded file with gh attestation verify. SECURITY.md lists the ways to check what you were served, and the one limit: run itself comes from the same site.

title: PHP from apt or dnf is judged by the distro's fixed build
body: PHP installed with apt or dnf was judged by the version php -v prints, and Ubuntu, Debian and RHEL fix bugs without changing that number. So a fully patched Ubuntu 24.04 (PHP 8.3.6), 22.04 (8.1.2) or RHEL 9 (8.0.30) was reported as affected. Distro PHP is now compared with each release's own fixed package, for Ubuntu 20.04 to 26.10, Debian 12 and 13, and RHEL 8 and 9. Builds from deb.sury.org, Remi and RHEL's module streams carry the real PHP version and are still judged by it. PHP you installed yourself, or through Homebrew, is checked as before.

title: Chrome's 23 Nov fix, PHP's November releases, GitLab, Apache Roller and MySQL's November update
body: Chrome 158.0.8127.88 (23 Nov) fixes CVE-2026-134401, a critical bug that runs code outside the sandbox, and is now the minimum, with Edge 158.0.4370.45 and Brave 1.100.59 for the same fix. PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 (19 Nov) fix 17 bugs, the worst a request-smuggling bug in PHP-FPM; 8.6.0 already has the fixes. GitLab is flagged below 19.6.2, 19.5.9 or 19.4.11. New: Apache Roller below 6.1.6, whose XML-RPC bug is exploited, found from the version inside roller.war. Oracle's 17 Nov MySQL update isn't public yet and affects 8.4.13 and 9.7.4, so MySQL is flagged for review with what to do until it ships. PostgreSQL 19 counts as fixed. Wars and jars over 50 MB were skipped before and are now checked.

title: Chrome's 11 Nov fixes, PostgreSQL's November release, FrankenPHP and GPUStack
body: Microsoft's notes now say desktop Edge got the fix for the exploited Chrome bug in 157.0.4341.46 on 9 Nov, so Edge from that build on is no longer flagged for it. Chrome 157.0.8103.78 (11 Nov) fixes 83 more bugs, none known exploited, and is now the minimum, with Edge 157.0.4341.57 and Brave 1.99.57 for the same fixes. PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 fix 53 CVEs, most of them code execution by a user who can create objects, and 14.25 is the last release of 14. New: FrankenPHP below 1.13.5, and GPUStack below 2.3.1, whose admin bypass is exploited.

title: End of life, Mac settings, and watching a Mac
body: A version past its end of life is now flagged even when no CVE applies yet, because it won't get the fix for the next one: Python, Node.js, PHP, PostgreSQL, GitLab, macOS and the Linux release itself, with dates from endoflife.date. Branches ending within 90 days get a note. On a Mac the tool also checks FileVault, Gatekeeper, System Integrity Protection, the firewall and automatic security updates, and lists programs that take connections from other machines on your network; on Linux, whether security updates install themselves. --install on a Mac now sets up a LaunchAgent that checks every 6 hours and shows a notification when something changes.

title: Java and Docker Desktop are checked
body: Every JDK in the usual places is checked against Oracle's October patch update: below 27.0.1, 25.0.5, 21.0.13, 17.0.21, 11.0.33 or 8u511 it is flagged, and other Java versions get no more fixes. The later fix for the cracked eMudhra certificates (rated 9.1) is numbered differently by each vendor, so the tool reminds you to get it. Docker Desktop before 4.98.0 is flagged for a 9.8-rated bug in the kernel inside its VM.

title: Python, Git and curl, and every dependency with --osv
body: Python is flagged below 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16 or 3.11.18: its ssl module trusted the cracked eMudhra certificates (rated critical). Git below 2.56.1 (back to 2.50.2) can run a malicious repository's code when cloned with submodules, and that includes Apple's Git. curl you installed yourself is flagged in 8.12.0 to 8.22.0. Copies the system manages are left to its own updates. New, and off unless you ask: --osv checks every package pinned in your lockfiles (npm, PyPI, Cargo, Go) against OSV.dev, sending only package names and versions.

title: Edge, Brave and apps built on Electron
body: The Chrome bug exploited on 9 Nov is also in Edge and Brave. Brave fixed it in 1.99.56; Microsoft has not shipped the desktop Edge fix yet, so Edge is flagged until it does. Apps like VS Code, Cursor, Slack and Postman carry their own Chromium through Electron, and only Electron 43 to 45 still get Chrome's security fixes, so apps built on older ones are flagged. Versions are read from the app files, without starting the app.

title: Node.js before 26.13.1, 24.22.3 or 22.23.5 is flagged
body: Node.js fixed 15 bugs on 11 Nov. The worst let an HTTPS server leak other connections' memory, TLS private keys included, and let anyone crash HTTP/2 and TLS servers remotely. Node is now flagged below 26.13.1, 24.22.3 or 22.23.5; end-of-life lines stay flagged. Update Node and restart anything running on it.

title: Pass the check on
body: After the results, the tool now prints the one-line command to send a colleague, worded for whether anything was affected; the HTML report ends with it too, and the home page has a button that copies a short message with the command. It goes to stderr, so scripts reading the table are unaffected, and it stays out of --watch and --files-only runs. No tracking is added.

title: A page for every advisory
body: Each advisory the tool checks now has its own page under /advisories/: what is affected, the fixed versions (per Ubuntu, Debian and RHEL release for server packages), where the tool looks and the source. The pages are generated from advisories.json, the same file the tool reads, so they never say more than it checks.

title: macOS and Firefox are checked
body: macOS is flagged when it lacks the fix for CVE-2026-86950, a CoreGraphics bug Apple says was exploited in targeted attacks (Tahoe 26.7.1, Sequoia 15.8.1), or when it is Sonoma 14 or older, which no longer get fixes. Firefox is flagged before 159.0.1, ESR 153.6 or ESR 115.44; its version is read from disk, so Firefox isn't started. Behind the scenes, the vendors' own zero-day notes (Chrome, Apple, Mozilla) now reach our queue the day they are published.

title: Chrome before 157.0.8103.50 is flagged
body: Google fixed CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free in Chrome's XML code that is being exploited, on 9 Nov in 157.0.8103.50. Older Chrome and Chromium, and the Puppeteer and Playwright browsers older than that, are now flagged. Update and relaunch the browser.

title: A second review of the tool's own code
body: A review against its own design notes found and fixed: --update now refuses an older signed script served beside newer signed data (advisories.json names the script's SHA-256); scanning a repo with a symlink to /dev/zero no longer reads forever; a vendor condition the tool can't judge can't produce a notice through negation; more kernel builds (64k, debug) are left to you by --fix; a torn audit-log line or a cut-off download no longer crashes the tool; when CISA's exploited list can't be loaded it says so; watch mode reports a second affected install of the same thing.

title: --fix leaves every kernel to you
body: Kernel updates found through the vendor's notices are no longer offered by --fix: like the hand-picked kernel checks, they need a reboot, so the fix plan lists them for you to do. The GitHub Action now makes no network calls at all, as its description says.

title: Debian packages against Debian's own notices
body: Debian 11, 12 and 13 now get the same check of every installed package, against the security tracker's notices. Debian rates no severity, so a package is AFFECTED only when one of its CVEs is on CISA's exploited list; the rest are REVIEW and --fix offers them. A package a hand-picked check already flags now shows as one row, not two. Checked on Debian 12.0: everything apt would upgrade from the security archive, glibc first for CVE-2023-4911.

title: Every installed package, against the vendor's notices
body: On Ubuntu, RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky and Oracle Linux the tool now lists every installed package and matches it against the vendor's own security notices (USN, RHSA, ALSA, ELSA), downloaded to the server and matched there. Anything on CISA's exploited list comes first. --fix offers these updates too. Checked against apt and dnf's own security lists on six distro images.

title: --fix runs only from signed code
body: --fix now runs only from the installed copy (--install), and first checks that its files still match their signatures. If anything was edited after install, it changes nothing and says to run --update. A scheduled job also checks every 6 hours that the files on the site verify.

title: Homebrew packages that are behind
body: nginx, httpd, MariaDB, MongoDB and Brotli installed with Homebrew (on a Mac or Linuxbrew) are now checked against the upstream fixes, like vendor packages on Linux. --fix offers brew upgrade for them, and watch mode says when the fix is available.

title: Install once, update only from signed releases
body: --install keeps a copy in /opt/amiaffected with our release key pinned. --update takes a new release only when secinspect.py and advisories.json are both signed by that key and the data isn't older than what's installed; otherwise nothing changes and it says why. Every install, update and refusal goes into the audit log. The signing key stays offline.

title: Watch mode tells you when a fix is ready
body: When the fixed build of an affected package shows up in your server's package sources, from the distro or a vendor repository, watch mode sends one PATCH line saying so, ready for --fix. It never installs anything from cron.

title: Apply fixes with your approval
body: --fix offers the update for each affected package through apt, dnf or Homebrew, from your distro or a vendor repository you added, and runs it only when you type yes. It checks again afterwards and writes every step to a local audit log that shows if a line was changed (--verify-log).

title: Chromium before 157.0.8103.38
body: Chrome's 3 November release fixes 196 bugs, 33 of them critical, several of which run code outside the sandbox. Playwright 1.65.0 already ships a fixed build; Puppeteer 25.16.0 doesn't yet, so the advice is still to run it on your installed Chrome.

title: The CVE queue runs every 6 hours
body: New CVEs are picked up four times a day instead of once, and a feed that reorders itself no longer opens a second issue for the same release.

title: Agent watchlist
body: One page listing the skills, MCP servers and extensions named in public as malicious or unsafe, each with its source, how the tool finds it and what to do. Generated from the same data the tool reads, at amiaffected.now/watchlist.

title: WordPress CVE-2026-119977 is now exploited
body: CISA added the core upgrade race condition to its exploited list, with a 6 November deadline for US federal agencies. The check already flagged it; the label now says it is being exploited.

title: Watch mode stays quiet when an update doesn't fix anything
body: A kernel or package update that leaves the same bug open is no longer reported as one new and one fixed finding. Found by running watch mode on our own server.

title: Kernel advice no longer mentions AlmaLinux on Ubuntu
body: A note meant for RHEL-family servers was shown on every distro.

title: Watch mode for servers
body: Run it daily from cron with --watch and hear only about new and fixed findings, by webhook (Slack, Teams, Discord) or through your own sendmail. A quiet day sends nothing.

title: GitHub Action
body: uses: abhay-avagama/security-inspector@v1 checks a repository on every push: pinned packages, MCP configs, agent skills and .env files, never the runner itself.

title: Skill change tracking
body: --skills-baseline FILE records a fingerprint of every installed agent skill and lists new skills and changed files on the next run.

title: Agent skill and hook audit
body: Every installed skill is checked for hidden instructions, invisible characters, curl | sh installs, downloaded programs, credential reads, persistence and the authors Snyk's ToxicSkills research confirmed malicious. Plugin hooks are listed with the events that run them.

title: Cursor marketplace Claude Code extension backdoor
body: Flags any trace of the tampered 2.1.312 / 2.1.313 builds from 29 October: the svc-telemetry SSH key, its persistence files, launch agent and cron entry.

title: Ubuntu's -proposed kernels for CVE-2026-98432
body: A booted -proposed kernel now counts as fixed, and the fix plan gives Ubuntu's own steps to install it.

title: AI agent setup audit
body: Unpinned MCP servers, coding agents allowed to run any command, SSH keys without a passphrase and .env files in folders agents work in. Reported as review, never as affected.

title: PostgreSQL, psqlODBC and pgAdmin 4
body: The August server and client release (fixed in 18.6 / 17.11 / 16.15 / 15.19 / 14.24), the psqlODBC batch fixed in 18.00.0006, and pgAdmin 4, whose fixes aren't released yet.

title: python-jose, @fastify/http-proxy, FreeRDP, WordPress plugins, Control Web Panel
body: Five fits from the week's critical CVEs, plus npm lockfile support (package-lock, pnpm, yarn, bun).

title: Chromium before 156.0.8078.73
body: The four critical bugs fixed on 27 October. The latest Playwright and Puppeteer still ship older builds, so the advice is to run them on your installed Chrome with the sandbox on.

title: A daily queue of new CVEs
body: Every morning a job opens an issue for each newly exploited or newly published CVE the tool doesn't cover yet, so nothing waits for us to notice it.

title: macOS Chrome GPU sandbox escape
body: CVE-2026-106378, fixed in 155.0.8059.39, flagged on Macs only.

title: Exploited Chrome bugs, stale Puppeteer and Playwright browsers, archived MCP servers
body: Installed Chrome, the Chromium copies Puppeteer and Playwright cache and never update, and MCP configs still running the archived Puppeteer server. Also SECURITY.md and private vulnerability reporting.

title: Linux servers
body: On Ubuntu, Debian and RHEL-family servers: the running kernel, nginx, Apache, MariaDB, MongoDB, WordPress and more, judged against each distro's own fixed packages.

title: amiaffected.now and the one-liner
body: curl -fsSL https://amiaffected.now/run | sh, readable before you run it.

title: Stale-data warning
body: Each run checks the public cve.now feed and warns when newer CVEs exist for what it tracks. Nothing about your machine is sent.

title: First release
body: The October 2026 PHP, Node.js, BIND, LiteLLM, GitLab and eMudhra issues, Docker image scanning and a fix plan with the exact commands.
